title: Allowlist
offline: The Machine is offline. The Allowlist can be changed once it is back online.
notAWall: The Allowlist is not a wall. An Agent that is talked into it can get around an entry, for example by editing the test script in package.json and then running the npm test that is on the list, or by setting core.fsmonitor in .git/config and running git status. The real wall is the sandbox and Egress (ADR 0030, 0008).

missing.title: Agent not found
missing.body: Its Machine may not have listed its Agents yet, or the Agent is gone.

runs.heading: Runs without asking for an Approval
runs.footer: Each entry is compared word by word from the start of the command: npm test covers npm test -- --watch. Commands joined with && ; | or & must pass on every part, and $( ), backticks and eval always ask. Reading and writing files is not on this list, because the sandbox holds it already.
runs.emptyDetail: Every command of this Agent asks for an Approval

add.heading: Add an entry
add.footer: An entry like git push covers git push --force origin main too, so keep it as narrow as you mean.
add.label: Command prefix

invalid.title: Cannot add it
invalid.body: Enter one command only, with no && ; or |, and no $( ), backtick or eval.

duplicate.title: It is on the list already

wide.title: {{entry}} is very wide
wide.message: The entry {{entry}} covers every command that starts with {{entry}}, whatever follows. Keep it as narrow as you mean, such as {{entry}} test.

try.heading: Try a command
try.label: Sample command
try.footer: Type a sample command to see whether the Agent runs it right away or asks first. If you typed a new entry above, the result counts that entry as added.
try.invalidDraft: The entry typed above cannot be added yet, so it does not count below.
try.runs: Runs without asking for an Approval
try.wouldRun: Would run right away if you add {{entry}}
try.asksAlways: Asks every time: the parts cannot be told apart reliably ($( ), backtick or eval)
